clue.text: Strikers on the march ? Pop gets into print

definitions.meaning: read literally, hitters marching past in procession
the published weekly ranking of pop records

explanation.surface: Striking workers march while a pop star makes the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the answer as HIT plus PARADE: people who strike, on the march. The second is its real sense, the chart of best-selling pop records printed each week.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of best-selling records is the pop listing, and literally a parade of hitters.

clue.text: Turner's come in for a top mark

definitions.text: Turner's come in for a top mark

parts.words: Turner's come in for a top mark
parts.note: the 'Turner' is the tide, which turns; when it has come in fully it leaves its highest line on the shore

explanation.surface: The painter Turner arrives to receive top marks for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner, but it is the tide, which turns. At its peak it leaves the high-tide mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point reached by a rising tide is marked on the shore as its top line.

clue.text: Mischievous dwarf causes the head to roll

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word just before

explanation.surface: A naughty little goblin threatens that heads will roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' is read as the first letter of 'the', T, which goes before ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scandinavian folklore trolls are mischievous dwarfs or giants living in caves and hills.

clue.text: How friendly of an overseas wellwisher to send a message!

parts.note: ami is French for friend, a wellwisher from across the Channel
to cable is to send a telegram

explanation.surface: A grateful exclamation at a kind message received from a friend abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' and 'of ... to' only frame the exclamation. A cable was a telegram sent by undersea wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable relations are good-natured and peaceable, the manner of people on good terms.

clue.text: Complete, Sir Anthony?

definitions.meaning: Sir Anthony ... is the domineering father in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the name is finished with Sir Anthony.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Anthony Absolute is a character in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's 1775 play The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total or unqualified, and is also the surname of Sheridan's knight.

clue.text: Mokes I assemble for the race

indicators.note: to assemble is to put parts together, so these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A gathering of donkeys is called together for a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mokes' (British slang for donkeys) and 'I' are rearranged; 'race' is a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit and related Arctic peoples were formerly called by this name, a people in the older sense of race.

clue.text: Fruit by the ton in a 28

annotationWithheld.why: Fruit by the ton in a 28 (5): cross-references 28-across, LAYER, but no reading of 'by the ton in a layer' builds APPLE
annotationWithheld.clue: Fruit by the ton in a 28

clue.text: Not partial to a bit of poetry ?

parts.note: a verse is a stanza or a line of a poem

explanation.surface: Someone declares they do not much care for poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means disliking it, the opposite of having a liking for it.

clue.text: Very powerful heavy drinker goes back in confined state

indicators.note: the turned drinker sits inside the word for confined

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in

indicators.note: going back means the drinker's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: A mighty drunkard is returned to custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes back' turns TOPER into REPOT, and 'in' places that inside PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepotent means having greater power or influence than others, predominant.

clue.text: Support needed when the lease runs out

indicators.note: running out suggests the word's letters coming loose and reforming in another order

explanation.surface: Help is needed when a tenancy agreement expires.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LEASE are rearranged; 'runs out' signals the change.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds up a painter's canvas or a blackboard.

clue.text: Old housewives' sweetmeats on 'TV

definitions.meaning: Goody was an old title for a married woman of humble rank
A British TV comedy series of the 1970s

explanation.surface: Grandmothers' confectionery is featured on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: the old title Goody for a housewife, sweet treats, and the 1970s BBC comedy The Goodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers treats and confections, matrons once titled Goody, and a trio of TV comedians.

clue.text: Rings for those who find them ?

definitions.meaning: a keeper ring is a plain band worn to hold a more valuable ring on the finger

explanation.surface: A remark about who gets to keep lost rings.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper is a ring that guards another; 'finders keepers' says things found belong to the finder.
explanation.definitionFit: Guard rings hold others in place, and the children's rule gives found things to the finder.

clue.text: She goes West, sorting mail

indicators.note: sorting the post rearranges it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman moves west, working on the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilma is a woman's name, so a female person, the referent of the pronoun.

clue.text: Soft warming drink

definitions.meaning: fine wool from young sheep is noted for softness
... was a hot spiced ale with roasted apples

explanation.surface: A gentle, comforting hot beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambswool is soft yarn, and also an old hot drink of ale, spice and apple pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine yarn is famously gentle to the touch, and the old wassail drink was served hot.

clue.text: Stand-in typist not here yet ? That's the pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
late means not yet arrived

explanation.surface: An office complains that the temporary typist has not turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a shaped guide used to copy an outline, a model to follow.

clue.text: Not the true way to improve a town

parts.note: to mend is to repair or put right
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A dubious recipe for urban renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is lying, a departure from honesty.

clue.text: Part of a plant for the table

definitions.meaning: a flat green growth from a stem
a hinged or removable board that extends a table

explanation.surface: A piece of greenery to decorate the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage grows on stems, and extra boards fitted to a dining table share the name.

clue.text: Matilda's might have saved her, if returned by a genuine member

indicators.note: returned means the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: real means genuine
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A remark about a rescue for Matilda, had a real limb come back.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hilaire Belloc's cautionary poem Matilda told lies, so when her house caught fire nobody believed her and she burned. 'Returned' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's liar raised false alarms, so a real warning of a blaze went unheeded.

clue.text: Not however used in shooting the rapids

definitions.text: Not however used in shooting the rapids

parts.words: Not however used in shooting the rapids
parts.note: a device named after a firearm that throws out spray, yet nobody uses it to go down white water

explanation.surface: A tool that has nothing to do with canoeing through white water.
explanation.walkthrough: Rapids throw up spray and shooting suggests a gun, but this tool sprays paint, not people down a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A paint sprayer is gun-shaped and creates a fine mist, yet has no place in canoeing.

clue.text: Devilish bad coil I shuffle off

indicators.note: to shuffle is to mix up, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A wicked person sheds this mortal coil, echoing Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Hamlet's 'shuffle off this mortal coil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolic means of or like the devil, fiendish.

clue.text: Army row grows coarse

definitions.meaning: soldiers stand in a ..., a line abreast
... describes plants growing thick and coarse; an adjective for a verb phrase

explanation.surface: A military quarrel turns vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers line up in rows, and rank vegetation is overgrown and coarse.

clue.text: A bob with the bookmaker goes fast

definitions.note: a verb phrase for the noun: one who runs fast

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s
a printer literally makes books

explanation.surface: A punter puts a shilling on with the bookie and quickly leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a British shilling (s). The bookmaker is not the racing bookie but a printer, who makes books.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-distance runner races at top speed.

clue.text: Such comics in the Chamber ?

parts.note: lurid frightening comic books, and the gruesome room of Madame Tussaud's waxworks in London

explanation.surface: A question about comedians in a parliamentary chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamber suggests Parliament, but it is the Chamber of Horrors at Madame Tussaud's London waxworks; comics are the lurid kind of comic book.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightening comic books form a genre, and the waxworks' room of murderers bears the same name.

clue.text: Heraldic Greek

parts.note: the Greek god who served as herald and messenger of Olympus

explanation.surface: A Greek coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldic suggests coats of arms, but it means acting as herald: the messenger god of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympian messenger carried the gods' announcements, their herald.

clue.text: A good clean TV serial ?

parts.note: drama serials were first sponsored by makers of detergent, so a clean-living show

explanation.surface: A wholesome television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio and TV serials were sponsored by detergent makers, hence the name; 'clean' plays on the soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-running domestic serials are named after the detergent firms that sponsored them.

clue.text: A nut case !

parts.note: literally the hard casing round a nut kernel, not a madman

explanation.surface: Someone is declared a lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer husk encases a nut's kernel.

clue.text: China tea ? Black ?

definitions.meaning: a tea grown in the Wuyi hills of China
it is a black tea, not green

explanation.surface: Someone asks for Chinese tea, without milk.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese leaf was a fine grade of black tea in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Bishop that unhappily came to nothing, thanks to mice

definitions.text: Bishop that unhappily came to nothing, thanks to mice

indicators.note: unhappily suggests something going wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A churchman met a sad end through rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Hatto of Mainz, in legend and Southey's ballad, was eaten by mice. 'Unhappily' rearranges THAT, and O for nothing follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary prelate was devoured by mice in his tower on the Rhine.

clue.text: A remark has some point with animals

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a pig is an animal
a ram is an animal

explanation.surface: A comment sharpened by mention of livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animals' gives two pieces, PIG and RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying.

clue.text: A festive cuppa for the nymph

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: A celebratory cup of tea is offered to a sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: Galatea is the sea nymph loved by Polyphemus, and the statue brought to life for Pygmalion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is a Nereid, one of the sea spirits.

clue.text: He shouts the odds-when beheaded?

annotationWithheld.why: He shouts the odds—when beheaded ? (5): 'He shouts the odds' defines LAYER, a bookmaker, but no clue word supplies the longer word that 'beheaded' would cut to LAYER

clue.text: With the boy in charge business at the peak goes with a bang!

parts.note: a son is a boy
a boom is a period of peak business activity

explanation.surface: With his son running it, the firm at its height expands explosively.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft breaking the sound barrier produce a loud explosive noise.
